properties.properties:
{'description': 'The historical repetition encoded in the Legends of "Kaelen of the First Dawn." The Sundered Paladin has existed before. The same conflict — a person containing both Light and Shadow, facing the choice between integrating or suppressing — has played out in previous generations. Each prior bearer of Oathbringer chose to "bind the shadow anew" (suppression), kicking the problem forward to the next generation. The Secret Outcome is the cycle's true exit condition: integration, not suppression.
', 'previous_iterations': 'The Legends of "Kaelen of the First Dawn" are fragmentary and treated as myth by most. Caius knows they are not. The cyclical nature means every solution the Order has deployed has been temporary — they have been managing symptoms, not treating the condition.
', 'the_order_as_perpetuator': "The Order does not know they are part of the cycle. They believe each iteration is unique. Their theological rigidity prevents them from recognizing the pattern because doing so would require acknowledging that their own ideology is one of the cycle's engines.
", 'the_exit_condition': 'The Secret Outcome — Kaelen and Eldrin integrating Light and Shadow rather than binding or unleashing — breaks the cycle because it removes the fundamental premise: that the two forces must be in opposition rather than dynamic equilibrium. Once integrated, the "choice" the prophecy describes no longer exists as a binary.
', 'the_cost': 'Every previous iteration ended with "bind the shadow anew." The world has been paying the accumulated interest on those decisions ever since — the Heartstone Network's degradation, the Ashen Wastes' expansion, the Order's rigidification. The cycle has a compound interest problem.
'}
{'domain': 'Character Mechanics & Physiological Toll', 'description': 'The physical and spiritual exhaustion experienced by a Lorekeeper when absorbing excessive corruption from allies.'}

{'description': "The primary spiritual conflict running through Kaelen's entire arc. Faith — in the Order, in his own goodness, in the possibility of redemption — vs. Doubt — in the Order's integrity, in his own nature, in whether a person who contains this much darkness deserves to survive it. The Shadow Self attacks specifically at this seam.
", 'the_stakes': "If Faith wins completely: Kaelen remains within the Order's framework, trusting institutions over personal experience. He becomes controllable. If Doubt wins completely: Kaelen loses the moral anchor that makes his choices meaningful. He becomes what the Shadow Self promises — pure power, no conscience. If Kaelen achieves synthesis: Faith in the right things (his companions, his own capacity for growth) combined with Doubt about the right things (institutions, inherited certainties) becomes discernment. This is the Weaver's final state.
", 'shadow_self_strategy': "The Shadow Self does not try to destroy Faith directly — it corrupts its target. It replaces faith in companions and self with faith in the Shadow Self's promises. It replaces doubt about the Order with doubt about everything, including Kaelen's own right to exist. The goal is not the absence of faith — it is faith in Nyx.
", 'the_order_version': 'The Order experiences this CAN institutionally: rigid Faith in doctrine that cannot accommodate doubt; therefore cannot learn, cannot grow, cannot respond to the truth when the Cover-Up collapses. Their collective inability to hold Faith-and-Doubt simultaneously is what makes them structurally fragile.
'}

{'full_text': '"The Sundered Paladin, bearing the blessed and cursed blade, shall face a choice: to bind the shadow anew, or to unleash the eternal night."
', 'surface_interpretation': {'order_reading': "Inevitable doom. Kaelen will fall to the Shadow Self. His corruption is a matter of when, not if. The only question is whether the Order can contain or sacrifice him before he becomes the instrument of unmaking. Justifies Valerius's control of Kaelen.
", 'valerius_reading': 'A roadmap for his ritual. If Kaelen's shadow can be drawn out (via Hand of Light) and contained, the prophecy resolves safely. His ritual is his attempt to force the "bind the shadow anew" outcome through a controlled extraction.
'}, 'true_meaning': 'Not a prophecy of doom but a roadmap to the Secret Outcome. The "key of bone and whispers" (Elara's Blue Stone Fragment + Eldrin's true voice) enable a third path: controlled integration of Light and Shadow. The "Sundered Paladin" is not broken — they are the one person who contains both forces and can therefore wield both consciously. The true resolution requires Kaelen and Eldrin (now allied within Oathbringer) to defeat the Shadow Self in the Inner World and fuse the two forces rather than suppress either.
', 'oakhaven_inscription': {'fragment_1': '"...When the Heart sleeps... the Shepherd... calls the flock to... the flame devoured..."
', 'fragment_2': '"...To silence the echoes... the shadow must be... embraced... or... chained anew by one who carries both light and..."
'}, 'historical_echo': 'The Legends of "Kaelen of the First Dawn" suggest this cycle has played out before. A previous bearer of Oathbringer faced the same choice — and chose to chain the shadow anew, kicking the problem forward to this generation. The Secret Outcome (fusion, not suppression) is the cycle's true exit condition.
', 'fragments': ['"...Kaelen of the First Dawn, once a beacon of light, now a vessel of shadow. His heart, once pure, now echoes with the whispers of the Stones..."
', '"...the circle holds, the arrows guide. Three paths to darkness, bound by will. Break the circle, loose the arrows, and Nyx shall feast..."
']}

{'origin': "An Eldorian ritual glyph developed during the Golden Age as a precision tool for channeling and balancing Heartstone energy. It was the Eldorians' most sophisticated magical instrument — capable of holding White Flame and Nyx energy in dynamic equilibrium. Requires a trained practitioner with Guardian bloodline attunement to use safely.
", 'canonical_form': 'Displayed at Whispering Stones in its original uncorrupted form', 'corrupted_usage': "The Cult of Nyx twisted the Symbol's design — reversing the flow direction so it acts as a siphon rather than a channel. Where the original draws energy from the Heartstone and redistributes it in balance, the Cult's version drains the Heartstone and feeds that energy directly into Nyx's bleed-through. Used at Oakhaven (carved into the square) to drain the Great Oak Heartstone during the Act I attack.
", 'prophecy_fragment': '"...the circle holds, the arrows guide. Three paths to darkness, bound by will. Break the circle, loose the arrows, and Nyx shall feast…" The "circle" is the Symbol of Binding; "break the circle" means corrupting the Symbol from a balance tool into a siphon.
', 'act_III_significance': "Understanding the Symbol's original function (balance, not suppression) is a prerequisite for the Secret Outcome — the controlled Light/Shadow integration requires a functioning, uncorrupted Symbol of Binding as a ritual anchor.
"}

{'nature': "Primordial, sentient force of Order, Creation, and Stability. The universal source of Light, hope, and structure. The White Flame is not a god — it has no personality, no agenda, no judgment. It simply is: the universe's tendency toward structure, preservation, and coherence. It is described as an ocean of which the Inner Flame is a personal drop.
", 'relationship_with_nyx': "Equal and opposite of Nyx. The two primordial forces were never intended to be in conflict — their tension was the generative engine of the world. ", 'relationship_with_inner_flame': "The White Flame is the external ocean; the Inner Flame is each person's personal drop of that ocean. The Order lost this knowledge.
", 'amplification': "The White Flame is amplified near healthy, functioning Heartstones. The degradation of the Heartstone Network has weakened its presence across the Shattered Lands — even Light magic is less reliable than it was in Eldoria's golden age.
", 'significance': "The Order treats the White Flame as a personal deity and moral absolute. The truth is more complicated and more beautiful: it is a force, like gravity, that can be worked with but not owned. The Order's ownership claim is their deepest theological error.
"}
